alt: 桌旁托盤裡放著幾座斷裂的模型，女孩仍神情堅定地組合新的橋樑支架，繼續嘗試。
scene_prompt: 不屈不撓 means steadfastly refusing to surrender in the face of difficulty and pressure. A modern school workshop, one determined older child persistently builds and repairs a small model wooden bridge. Several clearly FAILED earlier bridge prototypes with snapped balsa sticks and collapsed spans lie in a tray to one side. In foreground the child, with resolute focused expression, presses together a NEW strongly braced triangular bridge joint with both hands, continuing after setbacks instead of giving up. Fresh sticks, simple safe glue bottle without label, and a tabletop clamp sit ready; no dangerous saw or sharp tool. Through window a rainy gray sky contrasts warm hopeful work light. A friend farther back has put down a failed model with weary drooping posture, making the first child's determination more visible. Primary story is sustained effort through repeated failure, no trophies, no instant effortless success, no hardship injuries. Physically plausible small wooden construction: triangular truss pieces join coherently, hands grip actual sticks, exactly two arms per child, feet naturally planted beneath stools. No speech bubbles, written diagrams, letters, numbers or text.
